findings.claim: Across all cases reviewed, no department publishes a whole-front-door deflection rate; the only 'resolved without a lawyer' shares are NDA-specific, and only one case states its intake fields.
findings.detail: Synthesis across 20+ fetched case pages. Evidenced uses of intake data: single dashboard for resource allocation (Altria), status isolating outside-counsel wait (8x8), time-to-close and SLA reporting (Redwood), request-source visibility (CCEP), paper-type routing (Elastic), AI agent fallback to form (Altria). Any worked example for Article 2 must be a labelled composite from partial real numbers.
findings.source_title: Checkbox customer stories index (with Streamline AI, Josef, Juro and ACC pages listed in notes)

gaps: WebSearch budget was exhausted (200 of 200) before this task started: zero searches could be run, so the instruction to run at least 8 distinct searches could not be met. All work was done by direct WebFetch (about 60 fetches). Search-engine pages fetched via WebFetch were unusable (CAPTCHA, 429, 403, junk results).
ACC Value Champions 2024, 2025 and 2026 winner write-ups not reviewed: acc.com returned 403 on every route, including via a reader proxy; web.archive.org is not fetchable by the tool.
CLOC and LegalOps.com award winners not reviewed: legalops.com returned 403; cloc.org home page exposes no awards link.

CLOC Global Institute 2026 (Chicago, 11-14 May 2026) session descriptions not retrieved: agenda and daily pages render sessions client-side, returning navigation only. ACC Legal Operations session descriptions not reached.
CCBJ case articles not reached (site search returned an empty body). ACC Docket now redirects to corporatecounselnow.com, whose on-site search returned no results for 'intake' or 'value champions'.
World Commerce and Contracting benchmark on NDA cycle time and volume not found; no neutral NDA cycle-time benchmark located.

Gartner primary press release (2026-05-26) and the Gartner intake and triage case study both returned 403. Whether the original carries any methodology or population footnote is unverified; US-spelling original wording not seen.

No vendor metric is independently audited. Checkbox page dates (July-August 2026) appear to be site rebuild dates, so the true dates of those programs are unknown; Streamline AI and Josef pages are undated.
Sample size of the ACC / Everlaw 2026 survey not confirmed. Juro case metrics taken from index pages only. Ironclad, LawVu and Tonkean yielded no usable intake or self-service metric.
Liberty Mutual's self-service NDA tool is a pilot with no outcome data yet.
viewpoints: Analyst forecast view (Gartner): AI-driven intake answering half of requests without human intervention becomes majority practice by 2029; this is a prediction with no stated survey base, not evidence of current practice.

Practitioner view via ACC: current real programs are narrow and NDA- or template-specific, often built in-house (Liberty Mutual's Legal Data Science team, Palo Alto Networks on Gemini), with modest, honest metrics and pilots still running.
Vendor view: legal front door case studies emphasize adoption, speed of deployment and NDA volumes, and rarely disclose intake schema, total request volume or a whole-department deflection rate.
Measurement gap view (ACC / Everlaw 2026): most departments still do not track time to resolution, so the data that intake systems generate is largely unused for service reporting.
Process view (Elastic): most NDA delay sat upstream of legal review, in deciding whose paper to use, which suggests intake design, not lawyer speed, is the main lever.

gap:association-definitions-of-legal-ops.summary:
All four bodies were checked against primary text. WebSearch was exhausted and WebFetch refused verbatim output, so pages were fetched with curl and parsed locally. ACC's Maturity Model 2.0 was re-read from its PDF.

- **CLOC:** No one-sentence definition; describes legal ops professionals as "the chief operating officers of the legal team". Core 12 captured verbatim; last revised 7 April 2020, web copy modified May 2025.
- **ACC:** Definition and 14 functions captured verbatim. PDF created 29 September 2020, re-saved October 2024; the original model was 2017.
- **LegalOps.com:** Live site read directly; definition and mission match staging, but the live site has diverged. The 15 practice areas were read from an on-page image; per-area definitions are member-gated.
- **Legal Operators:** Publishes no definition or framework, only a content-tag list.

**Four topics:**
- Intake: not a function anywhere; only ACC names it, as a marker inside two functions. Self-service: absent from all.
- BI is a named function in each framework.
- KM is a named function everywhere and defined without AI by CLOC and ACC.
- AI appears once in CLOC (Technology) and four times in ACC, never in KM, and in no LegalOps.com area name. AI is entering through CLOC's September 2026 certification instead.

The organization behind RLLB is LegalOps.com (Brenton and Franke), not Legal Operators (McCarthy).

findings.claim: CLOC's 'What is Legal Ops?' page has no single-sentence definition. It frames legal ops by role: professionals who optimise 'the business and practice of law' and act as COO of the legal team.
findings.detail: Page blocks 'Legal Ops at its core / Allow lawyers to focus on providing legal advice' and 'An Evolving Role / So much more than outside counsel management'. It lists Strategic Planning, Financial Management, Project Management and Technology Portfolio Investment as example areas. It does not mention AI, intake, self-service or KM. Schema datePublished 2024-07-30, dateModified 2025-05-20. Raw HTML fetched with curl and parsed locally.
findings.source_title: What is Legal Ops - CLOC
findings.exact_quote: Legal ops professionals are the chief operating officers of the legal team.

findings.claim: The 12 Core 12 functions are: Business Intelligence; Financial Management; Firm & Vendor Management; Information Governance; Knowledge Management; Organization Optimization & Health; Practice Operations; Project/Program Management; Service Delivery Models; Strategic Planning; Technology; Training & Development. Each has a tagline and a two-sentence description.
findings.detail: All 12 taglines and descriptions are recorded verbatim in the notes file. Examples: BI 'Make better decisions through data'; Service Delivery Models 'Match the right work to the right resource'; Practice Operations 'Enable lawyers to focus on law.' Core 12 page datePublished 2024-07-30, dateModified 2025-05-16. Per-function pages datePublished 2024-09-27, dateModified 2025-05-06.
findings.source_title: Core 12 - CLOC
findings.exact_quote: Guide your organization with data, not intuition. Collect, organize, analyze, and visualize data to uncover trends, find efficiencies, and drive informed business decisions.

findings.claim: The Core 12 framework was last substantively revised on 7 April 2020, when CLOC replaced its original 'Core Competencies' with the current 12 functional areas. The names in that release match today's list.
findings.detail: CLOC's newsroom release matches the PR Newswire copy (Apr 07, 2020, 13:14 ET), with a Mary O'Carroll quote. Later layers: Core 12 Maturity Assessment Playbook (release dated May 1/2, 2024; four stages: Reactive, Emerging, Developing, Leading) and CLOC Compass (12 May 2026). The Compass release says 'The Core 12 has defined legal operations excellence since 2016.' The Internet Archive was offline, so I could not tell whether web wording changed at the 2024 relaunch or the May 2025 edits.
findings.source_title: CLOC Announces Updates To Its Core 12 Functions Of Legal Operations
findings.exact_quote: CLOC has updated its original CLOC Core Competencies to reflect the increased scope and priorities that today's legal operations professionals are responsible for.

findings.claim: CLOC's Knowledge Management function text does not mention AI. It defines KM as processes and standards to collect, structure and organise knowledge. The desired state adds taxonomies, automation and a sharing culture.
findings.detail: A local keyword count across all 12 function descriptions found 'AI' / 'artificial intelligence' once, on the Technology page only. KM desired-state bullets include 'with taxonomies to expedite retrieval of knowledge' and 'Implement automation to handle repetitive, low-value tasks and to mobilize organizational knowledge'. The page cites a 67% 'developing' KM maturity figure from 'the most recent CLOC State of the Industry Survey' without naming the edition.
findings.source_title: Knowledge Management - CLOC Core 12
findings.exact_quote: Implement processes and standards to collect, structure, and organize knowledge to save time and improve outcomes. Leverage existing knowledge to make work easier.

findings.claim: AI is mentioned once in the Core 12 function texts, in the Technology function's 'current reality' paragraph.
findings.detail: Technology desired-state bullets cover a multi-year roadmap, connecting platforms, automating high-volume processes, build-versus-buy, and 'Assess emerging technology capabilities and incorporate them into your long-term strategic planning'. No other Core 12 function text mentions AI.
findings.source_title: Technology - CLOC Core 12
findings.exact_quote: With the rapid advancement of technology, including developments with artificial intelligence, implementing new technology solutions, and automating legal processes are high priorities for most organizations.

findings.claim: CLOC's Business Intelligence function ends in dashboards, data lakes and 'advanced analytics'. It does not mention AI.
findings.detail: Current reality: 'In-house departments today often make minimal use of data and metrics.' Desired-state bullets: 'Determine the right data to collect and monitor'; 'Design and roll out metrics and dashboards'; 'Create data lakes and implement advanced analytics'; 'Spot patterns and identify hidden opportunities'. Note the slug is business-intelligence-2.
findings.source_title: Business Intelligence - CLOC Core 12
findings.exact_quote: Manage and guide your organization through data, not intuition.

findings.claim: The Core 12 has no intake, triage, 'legal front door' or self-service function. Across the 12 descriptions 'triage', 'front door' and 'self-service' never appear, and 'intake' appears once as a legal-project-management stage.
findings.detail: A local keyword audit ran over all 12 function pages, from 'Back to Core 12' to the resource listing. The single 'Intake' hit is in Project/Program Management. The nearest functions are Service Delivery Models, which covers sourcing mix rather than request intake, and Practice Operations. Strategic Planning notes that teams 'operate reactively to issues and incoming work requests'.
findings.source_title: Project/Program Management - CLOC Core 12
findings.exact_quote: recognized as a matter management framework for its alignment to the business of law over four lifecycle stages—Intake, Planning, Execution, and Review.

findings.claim: A CLOC-published blog post from March 2020 described Knowledge Management as building self-service legal solutions driven by AI and bots. Neither idea appears in the current Core 12 KM text.
findings.detail: The post 'Evolution of CLOC Core Competencies: Observations from a Maturing Market' is dated 2020-03-10, four weeks before the Core 12 update. It lists the 12 pre-2020 competencies: Financial Management; Vendor Management; Cross-Functional Alignment; Technology & Process Support; Service Delivery & Alternative Support Models; Organizational Design, Support & Management; Communications; Data Analytics; Litigation Support & IP Management; Knowledge Management; Information Governance & Records Management; Strategic Planning. The byline is a site account ('Johnny') and the text reads as a guest or vendor piece ('We've met with more than 50 clients'). Treat it as a CLOC-hosted blog post, not an official framework statement.
findings.source_title: Evolution of CLOC Core Competencies: Observations from a Maturing Market
findings.exact_quote: legal operations departments are creating on-demand, self-service legal solutions for their internal customers.

findings.claim: On 16 September 2026 CLOC announced the Legal Operations Certified Professional (LOCP) credential. It tests application of the Core 12 and explicitly covers AI. CLOC also announced 'CLOC Industry Standards' for public release at the 2027 Global Institute.
findings.detail: AI is entering CLOC's competency apparatus through certification and training, not through a rewrite of the Core 12 text. CLOC also launched an 'AI Intensive' on 19 August 2026; that date comes from a newsroom listing only. The LOCP release describes CLOC as 'Founded in 2015 as the organization that built the legal operations profession and defined its foundational framework, the CLOC Core 12'. Quote from Oyango Snell, President and CEO: 'CLOC built this profession'.
findings.source_title: CLOC Announces Industry-First Certification for Legal Operations Professionals
findings.exact_quote: apply the CLOC Core 12 in practice, work within ethical and regulatory frameworks including the Model Rules of Professional Responsibility, and account for the impact of AI transformation across the legal department.

findings.claim: ACC defines legal operations as activities that optimise legal services for corporations, rooted in business fundamentals and using processes, data and technology.
findings.detail: From the 'What is Legal Operations?' block on p.3 of the ACC Legal Operations Maturity Model 2.0. Second sentence: 'In many legal departments, this business management function is handled by dedicated legal operations staff that take responsibility for some or all of the areas in the ACC Legal Operations Maturity Model.' The PDF was re-read directly with pypdf because acc.com HTML pages return 403.
findings.source_title: ACC Legal Operations Maturity Model 2.0
findings.publisher: Association of Corporate Counsel (ACC Legal Operations)
findings.exact_quote: Legal operations disciplines are rooted in business fundamentals, leveraging processes, data and technology. They are designed to build consistency and drive efficiency and value in the practice of law.

findings.claim: ACC Maturity Model 2.0 has 14 functions, each assessed at three stages: early, intermediate and advanced. The functions are Change Management & Communication; Contract Management; eDiscovery; External Resources Management; Financial Management; Information Governance (Records Management); Innovation Management; Intellectual Property Management; Internal Resources Management; Knowledge Management; Metrics & Analytics; Project & Process Management; Strategic Planning & Legal Operations Leadership; Technology Management.
findings.detail: All 14 one-line definitions are verbatim in the notes file. Naming quirks inside the PDF: the TOC prints 'Metrics & Analysis' and 'Process & Project Management', while section headers print 'Metrics & Analytics' and 'Project & Process Management'. The IP definition says 'tangible assets' (sic). The model was crowd-sourced: 'Well over a hundred company representatives participated in the project.'
findings.source_title: ACC Legal Operations Maturity Model 2.0
findings.exact_quote: The Maturity Model attributes allow legal departments to place themselves in three stages of maturity in each function -- early, intermediate, and advanced

findings.claim: ACC Maturity Model 2.0 dates to 2020. The PDF's Info dictionary gives a creation date of 29 September 2020 (Adobe InDesign 15.0) and a modification date of 16 October 2024. The text says the original model was published in 2017.
findings.detail: PDF /CreationDate is D:20200929130821-04'00' and /ModDate is D:20241016123211-05'00'. HTTP Last-Modified is 17 Oct 2024. The 2010 XMP dates noted earlier belong to an embedded Illustrator logo asset. No ACC press release or page stating the launch date was reachable: acc.com returned 403, search engines blocked automated queries and the Internet Archive was offline. Cite as 'Maturity Model 2.0 (2020)'. I could not determine whether the October 2024 re-save changed content or whether a newer version exists.
findings.source_title: ACC Legal Operations Maturity Model 2.0 (PDF metadata and p.3 text)
findings.exact_quote: all stages are more advanced than when we published the original model in 2017.

findings.claim: ACC names intake and triage, but as a maturity marker inside Internal Resources Management and Technology Management, not as a function. 'Front door' and 'self-service' do not appear in the document.
findings.detail:
- Internal Resources Management, Early: 'Legal requests received by lawyers who delegate as needed'. The Intermediate bullet is quoted in exact_quote.
- Technology Management, Intermediate: 'Effort underway to digitize and automate processes (e.g. legal intake and triage, workflows, NDAs)'. Advanced: 'Systems typically include legal service intake/triage, legal hold...'.
- Nearest self-service ideas: Contract Management Advanced, 'playbooks allow extensive contract creation/execution with no legal department involvement'; Change Management Advanced, a business-facing component on 'how to access legal services'; KM Advanced, 'directories maintained and accessible by staff and clients'.
findings.source_title: ACC Legal Operations Maturity Model 2.0, pp. 21, 31-32
findings.exact_quote: Legal service request intake and triage function directing work to the appropriate resource in the Legal department

findings.claim: ACC's Knowledge Management function contains no AI. AI appears four times in the model, all at the Advanced stage: eDiscovery, IP Management, Metrics & Analytics and Technology Management. 'Generative' never appears.
findings.detail:
- KM definition: 'The process of capturing, distributing, and effectively using both structured and tacit knowledge assets, from work products (such as legal memos) to understanding of an issue due to prior experience.'
- KM Advanced: 'KM a standard component in organizational processes, supported by automated workflows'; 'Dedicated central repository to share knowledge'; 'At least one full-time dedicated KM professional'.
- AI mentions: eDiscovery, 'technology assisted review, predictive analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI)'; IP, 'Extensive use of artificial intelligence and machine learning across the lifecycle of patents and trademarks'; Technology Management, piloting 'artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotic process automation, and natural language processing'.
findings.source_title: ACC Legal Operations Maturity Model 2.0, pp. 23-24
findings.exact_quote: The process of capturing, distributing, and effectively using both structured and tacit knowledge assets

findings.claim: ACC frames metrics as the 'Metrics & Analytics' function. Its Advanced stage is self-service dashboards plus predictive analytics, and it says metrics 'support business intelligence'.
findings.detail: Definition: 'The system to collect, organize and use data to inform decision making and performance management.' Advanced: 'Department leaders directly access dashboards to filter data and answer questions to derive insights'; 'Decision making enhanced through use of predictive analytics (statistical techniques that include machine learning, AI, algorithms for data mining)'. 'business intelligence' also appears under Contract Management Advanced.
findings.source_title: ACC Legal Operations Maturity Model 2.0, pp. 25-26
findings.exact_quote: Metrics support business intelligence, driving continuous improvement in firm performance and selection, internal and external staffing, case assessment, and legal strategy

findings.claim: LegalOps.com's definition of legal operations management is confirmed verbatim on the live site, along with the statement that it identifies 15 core practice areas.
findings.detail: www.legalops.com returns 403 to WebFetch but 200 to curl with full browser headers, so the live page was read directly. The definition and the '15 core practice areas' sentence are on both live and staging /reference-modal. Live and staging text now differ on all three pages compared, so cite the live URLs. The page has no date metadata. Full models are member-gated ('Access the full models and in-depth guides when you become a member.').
findings.source_title: Legal Operations Reference Models & Frameworks
findings.exact_quote: Legal operations management is the oversight of how legal services are delivered across a department, ensuring they meet the right quality, cost, and risk thresholds for the enterprise.

findings.claim: LegalOps.com's 15 practice areas are: Commoditization of Legal Services; Knowledge Management; Records Management; Practice Area Enablement; Litigation Management Enablement; Performance Analysis; Technology & Process Enablement & Management; Communications Support & Management; Vendor Management; Legal Ops/Business Function Alignment; Strategic Planning; Financial Management; Service Delivery Solutions & Management; Legal Dept Org Design & Management; Data & Document Management.
findings.detail:
- The names exist only as an image on the live Reference Models page, which I viewed directly. HTTP Last-Modified on the image is 2026-07-04, which dates a site asset and not necessarily a model revision.
- A second image lists eight Leadership & Personal Effectiveness Skills: Self-Management & Self-Care, Leadership, Self-Knowledge, Communicating, Connecting, Collaborating, Influencing, Personal Brand.
- By name only: no intake or front-door area and no self-service area. 'Commoditization of Legal Services' sits at the apex and is undefined publicly. BI maps to 'Performance Analysis'. KM is a named area. AI is in no area name.
- Per-area definitions are gated, so deeper treatment is unverified.
findings.source_title: Legal Operations Management reference model graphic (on /reference-modal)

findings.claim: The live LegalOps.com About page carries a second, FAQ-style definition that refers to '12 core competencies'. This conflicts with the '15 core practice areas' on the Reference Models page and is absent from the staging mirror.
findings.detail:
- The FAQ 'What exactly is "Legal Operations"?' continues: 'This allows lawyers to focus on legal advice while the department operates with business-grade efficiency.'
- The mission sentence is confirmed live: 'We unite legal teams and providers to advance modern corporate legal services delivery through community, content, and data, not just events.'
- The Franke bio credits him with 'creating CLOC's 12 Core Competencies and LegalOps.com's Legal Operations Management Reference Model'.
- The Brenton bio mentions 'the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence'.
- The live homepage confirms 'three expert levels: Emerging, Established, and Industry Leader', which the earlier pass could not verify.
findings.source_title: About LegalOps.com
findings.exact_quote: Legal Ops is the multidisciplinary function that handles the "business of law." It encompasses 12 core competencies including financial management, vendor oversight, and technology implementation.

findings.claim: The LegalOps.com reference models were unveiled at the inaugural RLLB conference in October 2023. No later revision date is published.
findings.detail: LawVision (Susan Raridon Lambreth) partnered on the event, so it is an affiliated secondary source. Its post also says the Practice Areas model 'highlights 15 Practice Areas that represent the activities necessary for a legal department to deliver legal services with the ultimate objective of obtaining a competitive advantage for the business.' Schema datePublished is 2023-10-30.
findings.source_title: The Inaugural RLLB
findings.exact_quote: the unveiling two new reference models: LegalOps.com's Legal Operations Management Practice Areas and LegalOps.com's Leadership and Personal Effectiveness Skills.

findings.claim: Legal Operators (legaloperators.com) publishes no definition of legal operations and no competency framework. It is a community and events business whose closest structure is a content-tag list.
findings.detail:
- Pages read: /, /about, /membership, /innovation-hub, /events, /summit-by-the-sea-2025 and two /resource/ pages.
- The Innovation Hub offers 'over 38 different legal operations categories of interest' (36 visible), mostly technology labels. They include Artificial Intelligence, Automation, Business Intelligence Tools, Knowledge Management and Workflow Automation. There is no intake, front-door or self-service category.
- /about: 'Started in 2019 ... What originally started as a local meet up in a neighborhood bar has transformed into a national community.'
- Mission: 'to connect legal operations professionals globally with their peers and industry experts.'
- The footer reads (c) 2024 and the site still promotes Summit by the Sea 2025 (17-19 Sept 2025). Nothing dated 2026 was found.
- No mention of RLLB, 'Running Legal' or Brenton in the raw HTML of the three pages checked.
findings.source_title: About us - Legal Operators
findings.exact_quote: Legal Operators is the leading private community for legal operations professionals to connect with leaders, discover innovative solutions, and collaborate on solving problems.

findings.claim: Colin McCarthy is identified as founder of Legal Operators by a 2022 trade podcast, not by the organization's own site. His closest on-record 'definition' of legal ops is conversational.
findings.detail:
- Geek in Review Ep. 161 (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer) introduces him as 'CEO and founder'. In the auto-generated transcript he says the job is to 'operationalize the business of legal in house', starting with process, spend optimisation, 'looking at data analytics, measuring everything you do', diversity and technology. The transcript has errors ('spin' for 'spend'), so paraphrase rather than quote.
- He places the start in 2018 after first saying 2019; the site says 2019.
- The Legal Operators /about page does not name him. The Summit by the Sea 2025 page lists him as 'CEO and Founder at CMC Strategies'. His current role at Legal Operators is unconfirmed.
findings.source_title: The Geek in Review Ep. 161 - Colin McCarthy of Legal Operators on Building a LegalOps Community
findings.exact_quote: We asked the founder of Legal Operators, Colin McCarthy, to come on the show

findings.claim: 'The organization behind RLLB' means LegalOps.com, the company co-founded by CLOC co-founders Connie Brenton and Jeff Franke. It does not mean Legal Operators, the separate Colin McCarthy community whose flagship event is Summit by the Sea.
findings.detail:
- The conference site is a LegalOps.com subdomain titled 'RLLB Conference | Running Legal Like a Business', with a section 'Sessions Aligned with LegalOps.com Reference Models'.
- The live LegalOps.com navigation lists 'Annual Conference (RLLB)' and 'Sign Up for RLLB 2026'.
- LawVision calls it 'the inaugural LegalOps.com Running Legal Like a Business conference'.
- The live About page FAQ: 'LegalOps.com was co-founded by Connie Brenton and Jeff Franke ... Both were founding members of CLOC'.
- Legal Operators' site has no RLLB reference.
- A brief that attributes RLLB to 'Legal Operators' should be corrected to 'LegalOps.com'.
findings.source_title: RLLB Conference | Running Legal Like a Business
findings.exact_quote: Sessions Aligned with LegalOps.com Reference Models

gaps: ACC: no ACC-authored statement of the Maturity Model 2.0 launch date was reachable. The year 2020 rests on PDF metadata (created 2020-09-29) plus the PDF's 'original model in 2017' sentence. acc.com HTML returned 403 to curl, WebFetch and the Jina reader, and the Internet Archive was offline.
ACC: I could not determine whether the October 2024 re-save of the PDF changed content. I could not check whether ACC has issued anything newer than 2.0 or an AI addendum.
CLOC: I could not determine whether Core 12 web wording changed at the 2024 site relaunch or the May 2025 edits, because the Internet Archive was offline.
CLOC: the member-only Core 12 Maturity Assessment Playbook and the Compass tool were not read. How their stage descriptors treat intake, self-service, BI, KM or AI is unknown.
CLOC: the forthcoming 'CLOC Industry Standards' (announced for the 2027 Global Institute) are not public.
CLOC: the '67% developing' KM maturity figure on the KM page is not tied to a named State of the Industry edition.

LegalOps.com: per-practice-area definitions for the 15-area model are member-gated. Its treatment of intake, self-service, BI and KM is inferred from area names only. No revision date is published for the reference models. The October 2023 unveiling comes from LawVision, an event partner.

Legal Operators: there is no framework to analyse. Colin McCarthy's founder status rests on a 2022 podcast page, not on the organization's site. His current role is unconfirmed, and no 2026 content was found on the public site.

Search: the WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) and most public search engines blocked automated queries. Discovery relied on direct primary URLs, cloc.org site search, one successful Brave query and geeklawblog site search. A press release or trade article dating ACC 2.0 more precisely may exist but was not found.
viewpoints: CLOC defines legal ops by role and stature: 'chief operating officers of the legal team' and 'strategic business partner'. Its framework is a list of 12 functional areas. In the September 2026 certification release CLOC says it 'built this profession' and 'defined its foundational framework, the CLOC Core 12'.

ACC defines legal ops as a business-management discipline ('rooted in business fundamentals, leveraging processes, data and technology'). Its framework is a crowd-sourced, three-stage maturity model across 14 functions. It is the only one of the three that names intake and triage, and the only one with standalone Contract Management, eDiscovery, IP Management, Innovation Management and Change Management functions.

LegalOps.com (Brenton and Franke) defines legal operations management by outcome thresholds ('quality, cost, and risk thresholds for the enterprise') and frames the end goal as competitive advantage. It claims lineage over the CLOC framework: Franke's bio credits him with 'creating CLOC's 12 Core Competencies'. It positions its reference models against communities that 'focus on basic networking'.
Legal Operators takes no definitional position. It presents itself as a peer community ('content, connections, and tech') and organises content by technology category rather than by competency.

Common blind spot: all three published frameworks were written before generative AI (2020, 2020 and October 2023). None treats intake / the legal front door or self-service as a function, and both CLOC and ACC define KM without AI. AI is now arriving through adjacent programmes (CLOC's LOCP credential and AI Intensive; RLLB's 2026 AI track) rather than through revised framework text.

Lineage tension: CLOC's 2026 releases say it was 'Founded in 2015' and that the Core 12 has defined excellence 'since 2016'. LegalOps.com says Brenton and Franke 'founded ... CLOC in 2016' and that Franke created the original 12 competencies. An article citing both should attribute carefully and avoid taking sides on who 'built' the profession.

gap:conference-session-sweep-2026.summary: WebSearch was unavailable (session budget 200/200 already spent; all three attempts refused), so I ran zero general searches and relied on ~45 direct fetches of primary pages and on-site search pages of the named outlets. Load-bearing sources were read as raw page/PDF text, so quotes are verbatim. Filled: (1) CLOC CGI 2026 full official agenda (117 items) with titles, speakers, orgs for data/BI, KM and intake sessions; post-event release (nearly 2,400 attendees; Snell quote). (2) Harbor 2026 Legal Department Maturity Index press release verified: 98% implementing/exploring AI, 57% live, 24% pilot, 81% rank technology top priority; sample size NOT disclosed. (3) CLOC Compass launched 2026-05-12 (Core 12, four stages, members-only beta); no findings published. (4) ILTACON 2026: 5,780 attendees; session catalog not public; Artificial Lawyer/Draftwise daily briefings, Harbor's 2026-09-11 brief (KM sessions: clean connected data precondition; AI governance ownership fragmented across IT, Risk, GC, KM), three CCBJ pieces, LawSites round-ups (Entegrata semantic layer, NetDocuments context graph). (5) ILTA 2026 Technology Survey public executive summary (508 firms; 94% engaged with GenAI; knowledge infrastructure "dramatically underdeveloped"; firms anticipate KM and data-science headcount). (6) RLLB: one new trade-press recap, CCBJ 2026-09-18, with iFood intake example. Not retrieved: ACC 2026 Annual Meeting (acc.com 403), RLLB keynotes/awards, LinkedIn recaps, Legal IT Insider.

findings.claim: Harbor's 2026 Legal Department Maturity Index Survey (released at CLOC CGI, 11 May 2026) reports 98% of legal departments implementing or exploring AI, 57% live and 24% in pilot; sample size is not disclosed.
findings.detail: Press release read verbatim from raw HTML. Also: 81% of departments rank technology as primary operational focus for 2026. No methodology, n, or field dates given; no standalone report page on harborglobal.com (sitemaps checked). A CGI session description says Harbor's AI maturity workshop used data from the 2025 Harbor Law Department Survey with CLOC (135 departments), so the Index may be a re-cut, but this is not stated. Do not print n=135 for the Index.
findings.source_title: New Harbor Research Finds Legal Departments Surging Ahead on AI, but Operating Model Gaps Are Limiting Scale
findings.exact_quote: 98% of legal departments report implementing or exploring AI, with 57% already live and 24% in pilot.

findings.claim: Harbor's Kevin Clem frames the next phase of legal department maturity as an operating-model problem, not a technology problem.
findings.detail: Kevin Clem, Executive Vice President, Client Engagement, Corporations at Harbor. Release also states: 'Technology is in place. The operating model has not kept up.' and that outside counsel demand is becoming 'more selective, more data-driven, and more value-focused.'
findings.source_title: New Harbor Research Finds Legal Departments Surging Ahead on AI, but Operating Model Gaps Are Limiting Scale
findings.exact_quote: The next phase of maturity will be defined by how well organizations align technology, workflows, talent, and governance into a cohesive operating model.

findings.claim: CLOC Global Institute 2026 (May 11-14, Chicago) drew nearly 2,400 attendees from 26+ countries with 90+ sessions; CLOC's CEO characterised the shift in AI conversation as moving to what broke and how to govern it.
findings.detail: Theme 'Stronger by Design'. Headline says 'More Than 2,300', body says 'nearly 2,400'. Release lists 'data-driven decision making' among session themes. Keynotes: Zack Kass ('The Next RenAIssance'), Second City Works, Judd Kessler (Wharton). Verified on raw page text.
findings.source_title: 2026 CLOC Global Institute Brings More Than 2,300 to Chicago as Legal Operations Profession Claims Its Seat at the Table
findings.exact_quote: A year ago, the conversations at CGI were about what AI might do. This week, they were about what it has done, what broke, and how we govern it.

findings.claim: The only practitioner-led AI-era KM breakout at CGI 2026 was 'Supercharge Legal Operations: Harness Legal Knowledge Like Never Before', led by JPMorganChase and Guggenheim legal ops/KM staff, including an in-house KM librarian.
findings.detail: Tue May 12, 2:15 PM. Speakers: Jamal Brown (Head of Legal Operations, Guggenheim Investments); Sadie Khodorkovsky (Managing Director eDiscovery Legal Operations and Knowledge Management, JPMorganChase); Leslie Jordan (Knowledge Management Librarian, JPMorganChase); Jen Hugo (VP Legal Operations, JPMorganChase). Tagged Core 12: Business Intelligence, Knowledge Management, Strategic Planning, Technology. Description mentions knowledge powering 'self-service support'. Separately, the CLOC Academy 200-level KM workshop (Ben Clemson, AustralianSuper) has a description that never mentions AI. Source is the official agenda data feed behind globalinstitute.cloc.org/full-program.
findings.source_title: CLOC Global Institute 2026 Full Program
findings.exact_quote: Currently, legal operations struggle with fragmented information and missed collaboration opportunities.

findings.claim: CGI 2026's strongest in-house BI case study was Westpac Legal's 'Fix, Grow, Run, Transform - the executive report', describing an executive dashboard answering 'What do you Pay?' and 'What do you Get?'.
findings.detail: Tue May 12, 3:00 PM. Speakers: Petra Stirling (Director, Operations, Risk and Transformation, Westpac Group Legal) and Steven Robert (Executive Manager - Data & Technology, Westpac). 30+ practice areas, 200 lawyers, 'semi-automated data platforms and BI tools'. Other data sessions: 'Must Know Session: The CLOC + Harbor State of the Industry Survey' (Lauren Chung, Harbor; Stacy Lettie, Organon; Greg Bennett, Workday); 'From Invoices to Insight' (Wolters Kluwer, Brightflag, DHL, Atlassian); 'The Great Pricing Reset' (Mike Haven, Meta; Ilona Logvinova, HSF Kramer; Basha Rubin, Priori); 'Beyond the Cost Center Myth' (Ironclad, CoverMyMeds); 'Benchmark Your Legal AI Maturity' (Harbor, Uber, Docusign).
findings.source_title: CLOC Global Institute 2026 Full Program
findings.exact_quote: Westpac Legal leverages semi-automated data platforms and BI tools to showcase how legal enables the business to Fix, Run, Grow, and Transform.

findings.claim: At CGI 2026, intake and self-service content was mostly vendor-presented 'Legal Hack' slots (Checkbox 'Legal Front Door', Legora Portal, OpenText), plus an HPE low-code intake workshop.
findings.detail: Checkbox AI (Evan Wong listed), Wed May 13 2:00 PM: 'The Legal Front Door: The Foundation You Need Before AI Can Deliver'. Legora (Daniel Free, Jonathan Williams), Wed May 13 11:15 AM: 'Legal self-service for your business with Legora Portal' - external counsel share playbooks, 'transforming advisory work into reusable, scalable legal knowledge'. HPE (Dan Stangel, Kacy McCallister), Tue May 12: builds 'a simple but powerful Legal Request Intake tool' with Power Apps and SharePoint. 'Beyond the Buzz: Building and Deploying AI Agents in Legal Ops' (Morgan Lewis, Microsoft, HSBC) lists 'Contract intake, triage, and redlining assistance' as an agent workflow. The 'mostly vendor-led' characterisation is my inference from the agenda.
findings.source_title: CLOC Global Institute 2026 Full Program
findings.exact_quote: most AI investments are focused on executing legal work, not managing how that work is captured, triaged, prioritized, and delivered.

findings.claim: CLOC Compass launched at CGI on 12 May 2026 as a members-only beta maturity assessment across the Core 12 with four stages (Reactive, Emerging, Developing, Leading); no aggregate findings have been published.
findings.detail: Built with Neota Logic; 12 modules of 5-10 minutes each. Page says benchmarks come from 'anonymized, aggregated data across participants' but no participant count or distribution is public as of 2026-09-21. CGI working session: 'The CLOC Compass: Navigate Your Legal Department Maturity' (Dr. Amy Thomsen, CLOC; Kevin Bielawski, Husch Blackwell; Lindsay Staples, Beta Technologies; Neota staff). Compass page and launch release were read via the summarizing fetch tool only.
findings.source_title: CLOC Compass
findings.exact_quote: How do we know how we're doing, and what does 'better' actually look like for our function?

findings.claim: ILTACON 2026 (Aug 23-27, Nashville) was the largest ever: ILTA reports 5,780 attendees and 241 booths; LawSites reported registrations of 5,700 versus 4,600 in 2025 and called it 'peak legal tech'.
findings.detail: Ambrogi figures verified on raw page text: 29 countries; 2,803 Gaylord rooms sold out. He observed the floor theme was partnerships and integrations ('everyone is MCP-ing, API-ing'). ILTA wrap-up page (5,780; 'over 80 educational sessions' per agenda overview) read via summarizer only. The ILTACON 2026 session catalog is not publicly available; the agenda page links to a stale 2023 spreadsheet.
findings.source_title: Have We Reached 'Peak Legal Tech?' Sure Felt That Way At ILTACON this Week
findings.exact_quote: As of Wednesday, registrations had reached 5,700, 1,100 more than last year's 4,600

findings.claim: At ILTACON 2026 day one, a taxonomy/data-structure session (Heath Harris, NetDocuments; Ivy Grey, iManage) argued that well-structured data makes AI more efficient, that 'more is not better' in taxonomies, and that librarians are an existing source of expertise.
findings.detail: Reported by Will Seaton (Chief Customer Officer, Draftwise) as special correspondent for Artificial Lawyer; vendor-authored trade coverage. Reporter's conclusion: 'Taxonomy is becoming a much more central part of the AI conversation.' Session title not given. Other named sessions: 'Platform Wars: Which AI Tools Do Lawyers Really Want?' and 'Whose Legal AI Workflow Is It Anyway?'. Verified on raw page text.
findings.source_title: ILTACon 2026: Day One Briefing
findings.exact_quote: They understand how information is supposed to work together.

findings.claim: ILTACON 2026 speakers reframed AI value measurement: Tim Fox (Ogletree Deakins) described a move from efficiency to enablement, and James Ding (Draftwise) said the point of measurement is better decisions.
findings.detail: Day Two (2026-08-26): Tim Fox, Chief Data & AI Officer, Ogletree Deakins: 'We're switching from efficiency to enablement, talking more about what you can do with AI instead of just how much time is saved.' Day Three (2026-08-27): James Ding: 'The point is not data science. The point is better decision-making.' Igor Labutov (Epiq) on joining procurement, contract and disputes data: 'that unlocks a whole new set of value propositions.' Both briefings written by the Draftwise team; verified on raw text.
findings.source_title: ILTACON 2026: Day Three Briefing
findings.exact_quote: The point is not data science. The point is better decision-making.

findings.claim: Harbor's ILTACON 2026 recap says KM and marketing-technology sessions converged on clean, connected data as the precondition for AI, and that roundtables reported AI governance ownership fragmented across IT, Risk, the GC's office and knowledge management.
findings.detail: Author Justin Farmer, Practice Group Leader, Enterprise Solutions, Harbor; dated 11 Sep 2026. Also: 'Stop reporting logins and usage rates'; recommends governing 'only the data behind a specific, recurring deliverable' and expanding; cites Harbor's own finding that 0% of participating top-tier firms and global in-house departments have a mature AI impact measurement framework, despite a 41% rise in average annual law firm software spend 2021-2025. Harbor is a consultancy; the 0% figure is its own research and has been questioned elsewhere for methodological transparency.
findings.source_title: ILTACON 2026: Why AI usage isn't the same as AI value
findings.exact_quote: A recurring theme across ILTACON's marketing technology and knowledge management sessions was that clean, connected data is the precondition for AI producing anything useful.

findings.claim: ILTA's 2026 Technology Survey public executive summary (508 firms) says 94% of firms are engaged with GenAI (up 14 points), that knowledge infrastructure remains 'dramatically underdeveloped', and that firms anticipate added headcount in KM and data science; it gives no data on who leads AI programs.
findings.detail: PDF read directly. 508 firms, 139,000+ lawyers, ~275,000 users; released 2026-09-14/15. Authors Rich Raether (Quarles & Brady), Andrew Medeiros (Troutman Pepper Locke), Todd Corham. Other lines: 'Many firms anticipate additional headcount needs across IT, innovation, security, training, knowledge management, and data science.'; 'The platform migration is largely complete, but the governance migration has yet to begin.'; tracking/compliance tools in use by 'less than one-in-five firms'. Law firms only. KM-role detail, if any, is in the members-only full results.
findings.source_title: The ILTA Technology Survey: 2026 Executive Summary
findings.exact_quote: knowledge infrastructure remains dramatically underdeveloped across enterprise search, expertise management, pricing, procurement, and competitive intelligence.

findings.claim: CCBJ's ILTACON interviews capture the DMS-vendor view that models are 'rented' while institutional context is permanent, and that AI has returned KM to taxonomy; iManage flags corporate legal departments as having weaker matter records.
findings.detail: Three Kristin Calve pieces dated 2026-08-31. NetDocuments CEO Josh Baxter: an Am Law 20 firm had 48 AI applications 'that they know of'; per-app copies become 'micro and incomplete DMSs'. Heath Harris: 'How do I turn millions of documents into a structured database?'. iManage's Paul Walker: 'We're right back at taxonomy' and matter centricity 'makes the AI safe to operate'; on corporates: 'It'll be interesting when we turn it on on some corporates to see how that story meanders'. Calve: 'The bottleneck may not always be model quality; it may be record quality.' She labels NetDocuments' 48% cost-per-correct-answer figure 'a vendor-run benchmark'. Second URL: https://ccbjournal.com/blog/matter-centricity-2-0-legal-ai-rediscovers-the-matter
findings.source_title: Rented Models, Enduring Memory
findings.exact_quote: That intelligence, that context, that's going to have a place of permanence.

findings.claim: Law-firm data platforms announced at ILTACON 2026 converged on 'semantic layer plus MCP server': Entegrata doubled to 20 firm clients, launched a Metrics semantic layer, and says the dedicated data layer debate is over.
findings.detail: LawSites round-up part 3 by Bob Ambrogi. Entegrata added Cleary Gottlieb, Wilson Sonsini, Kilpatrick Townsend; 50+ connectors; 'nearly one billion rows of data daily' (company claim). NetDocuments says its Legal Context Graph 'cut the cost per correct answer by 48% while maintaining accuracy' (vendor benchmark). Part 4 covers Litera Firm AI Search, Oddr MCP server for AR/DSO queries, Aderant Agent Center, Intapp-Legora (summarizer only). The 'semantic layer plus MCP' pattern is my synthesis.
findings.source_title: ILTACON News Round-Up Part 3, Documents, Data and AI
findings.exact_quote: A year ago, a lot of firms were still debating whether they needed a dedicated data layer. Now they are competing on how fast they can release one

findings.claim: A trade-press RLLB 2026 recap published 18 Sept 2026 (CCBJ) reports an intake/self-service example from iFood in which low-risk contract appendices proceed with no human in the loop, and argues legal work allocation is being embedded into rules and thresholds.
findings.detail: Kristin Calve, Editor, CCBJ (historically an RLLB media partner). Named speakers: Karen Helten (Outside Counsel Senior Manager, Salesforce) and Camila Nagano (Head of Legal and DPO, iFood) on one stage; an agentic AI workshop; a panel of Deborah Haile (Uber), Daniel Neises (Snap), Jean Yang (Onit), Sam Bernstein (Davis Wright Tremaine) on whether clients should require, regulate or preclude law-firm AI use. Session titles not given. Also: 'Legal operations, procurement, sourcing, finance, knowledge and technology professionals increasingly help choose providers, establish criteria, define workflows and write the instructions agents follow.' No statistics. Verified on raw page text.
findings.source_title: The Quiet Rewiring of Legal Work
findings.exact_quote: At iFood, a contracting process can move a request from Slack through Salesforce data and Jira toward e-signature, with certain low-risk appendices proceeding without a human in the loop.

findings.claim: CCBJ's ILTACON 2026 editorial argues the durable value in legal AI is institutional knowledge and entitlement data rather than models, and that the week's real question was cost-justified quality.
findings.detail: Kristin Calve, 2026-08-31. 'What they cannot swap out so readily is what surrounds them: decades of documents, matter histories, work product and institutional knowledge and a clean answer to who is entitled to see what.' and 'value doesn't disappear with the interface. It settles deeper into the stack.' No sessions or statistics named.
findings.source_title: At ILTACON, Legal AI Confronts 'Good Enough'
findings.exact_quote: How much better does the result need to be to justify paying more for it?

findings.claim: An ILTA blog post (11 Sept 2026) on Big Law AI organisation cites new roles such as Director of Artificial Intelligence, Legal Engineer and Data Scientist, plus statistics whose underlying sources I could not identify.
findings.detail: Authors Damian Priamurskiy and Julianne Kasprzyk Crowley (Lowenstein Sandler). Post cites legal-AI job postings up 340% Jan 2024 to Jan 2026 and 78% of Am Law 200 firms with at least one AI-focused position; sources not traced, read via summarizer only. It does not name KM teams as AI program leaders. Do not use the statistics without tracing them.
findings.source_title: From Innovation Labs to Embedded Intelligence: How AI Is Reshaping Big Law

ILTA KM community: no 2026 KM white paper, KM survey, or statement on KM team roles in AI programs was found; the executive summary's only KM-role statement is that firms anticipate added KM headcount, with no percentage. Full survey results are members-only.

Only new item is the CCBJ piece of 2026-09-18.

Items read only through the summarizing fetch model (ILTA wrap-up page, ILTACON keynotes page, CLOC Compass pages, LawSites round-up part 4, two ILTA blog posts) should have wording re-verified before quotation.
viewpoints: Association view (CLOC, Oyango Snell): the AI conversation has moved from what AI might do to what it has done, what broke, and how to govern it; legal ops is building, proving and leading.

Consultancy view (Harbor: Kevin Clem, Justin Farmer): adoption is near-universal but the operating model lags; measure outcomes not logins; govern data one recurring deliverable at a time; AI governance needs a single clear owner because ownership is fragmented across IT, Risk, GC and KM.

DMS-vendor view (NetDocuments' Josh Baxter and Heath Harris; iManage's Paul Walker and Ivy Grey): models are rented and interfaces swap out, institutional context is permanent; AI has sent the industry 'right back at taxonomy'; librarians and KM staff hold the needed expertise; bring the application to the knowledge.

Data-platform vendor view (Entegrata's Tom Baldwin): the debate over a dedicated data layer is over; firms now compete on speed to ship one, with semantic layers and MCP servers exposing governed data to any AI tool.

Law-firm practitioner view (Tim Fox, Ogletree Deakins): shift value talk from efficiency to enablement; firm-wide time-savings totals are noise unless connected accurately in the data; every AI workflow keeps a human in the loop.

In-house practitioner view (iFood and Salesforce at RLLB; Westpac and JPMorganChase at CGI): embed risk thresholds into intake flows so low-risk work proceeds without lawyers; use invoice data to allocate outside counsel work; build executive dashboards that answer what legal costs and what it delivers; treat KM as AI-enabled knowledge discovery.

Trade-press analyst and sceptic view (Kristin Calve, CCBJ; Bob Ambrogi, LawSites): the real question is cost-justified 'good enough'; value settles deeper into the stack with institutional knowledge and entitlements; vendor benchmarks should be read as vendor benchmarks; 'peak legal tech' spending signals capital misallocation.

Survey-author view (ILTA 2026 Technology Survey): platform migration is largely complete but the governance migration has yet to begin; knowledge infrastructure is dramatically underdeveloped; success depends on process discipline, data strategy and systems integration rather than GenAI itself.

gap:bi-technology-state-and-deterministi.summary:
IMPORTANT METHOD LIMIT: WebSearch was refused (session budget of 200 already spent), and public search engines fetched via WebFetch were blocked. I ran zero keyword searches. Instead I retrieved about 75 primary pages directly (vendor docs, newsrooms, release notes, analyst blogs, plus on-site searches/indexes) and copied every quote from the downloaded page text (curly quotes normalised). gartner.com, tableau.com marketing pages and powerbi.microsoft.com were HTTP 403, so no Gartner text was read; 2026 Magic Quadrant content is vendor characterisation only.

Findings: (a) As of Sept 2026 the conversational layer is GA at Tableau (Next GA 2025-04-15; Tableau Agent conversational GA 2026-05-05), Databricks (Genie GA 2025-06-12; Genie Spaces renamed Genie Agents 2026-07-08), Snowflake (Intelligence and Cortex Agents GA 2025-11-04; Cortex Analyst being folded into Cortex Agents 2026-08-28), Looker (GA "last year") and Fabric data agents (GA 2026-03-18). Power BI's report Copilot pane is GA but the standalone Copilot is still preview. (b) OSI launched 2025-09-23, entered Apache incubation 2026-06-22 as Apache Ossie, 50+ organisations, spec still a 0.2.0 draft. dbt's April 2026 benchmark: semantic layer 98 to 100% vs text-to-SQL 84 to 90%. (c) "Deterministic" is vendor language (dbt, Looker, ThoughtSpot, Tableau Pulse); Forrester says shared semantic layer as enterprise infrastructure; BARC is a counterweight. Power BI Copilot can author new DAX, so "call, never recompute" is not universal. (d) Microsoft: 30M+ monthly users (Sept 2025), 35M (Mar 2026). (e) Alert-to-workflow patterns documented for Power BI, Activator, Tableau, Looker, ThoughtSpot.

findings.claim: Power BI Copilot release status is mixed as of late August 2026: the in-report Copilot pane is GA, the standalone cross-item Copilot and Copilot in apps remain preview, and Copilot requires Fabric F2+ or Premium P1+ capacity (Pro or PPU licence alone is insufficient).
findings.detail: Microsoft Learn 'Overview of Copilot for Power BI' (ms.date 2026-08-24, updated 2026-08-31). Second quote on same page: 'The Power BI agent available as a standalone, full-screen experience accessible from the Power BI left navigation is in preview.' Standalone page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-chat-with-data-standalone, last updated 2026-08-27) is still titled '(preview)'. 'Prep data for AI' (verified answers, AI instructions) also still preview.
findings.source_title: Overview of Copilot for Power BI
findings.exact_quote: The report agent Copilot pane available on the right side of reports is generally available.

findings.claim: Power BI Copilot prefers governed semantic-model measures but can also generate new DAX, so it is not a strict 'call the governed metric, never recompute' design.
findings.detail: Important nuance for the deterministic thesis. From the standalone Copilot doc (ms.date 2026-07-06, last updated 2026-08-27). Same doc warns that unprepared models give 'limited or inaccurate' answers and that models not approved for Copilot show a low-quality warning.
findings.source_title: Standalone Copilot experience in Power BI (preview)
findings.exact_quote: it then uses the measures and other data fields in your semantic model (or even creates new DAX calculations) to generate the answer for you.

findings.claim: Fabric data agents are generally available (announced 2026-03-18), are strictly read-only, can use Power BI semantic models and ontologies as sources, and can be invoked from Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Foundry and Teams.
findings.detail: GA announcement by Arun Ulag on Azure Blog 2026-03-18: 'I'm excited to share that Fabric data agents are now generally available.' Microsoft Learn concept page (ms.date 2026-05-11, updated 2026-09-09) confirms GA and says: 'The Fabric data agent strictly enforces read-only access, maintaining read-only data connections to all data sources.' Up to five sources per agent; NL2SQL, NL2DAX, NL2KQL. Doc suggests routing 'questions about financial metrics to a Power BI semantic model'.
findings.source_title: Fabric data agent concepts
findings.exact_quote: Data agent in Microsoft Fabric is a generally available feature that enables you to build your own conversational Q&A systems by using generative AI.

findings.claim: Tableau Next and Tableau Semantics became generally available on 2025-04-15 (Tableau+ SKU).
findings.detail: Salesforce newsroom announcement. Same page: 'Tableau Semantics serves as the semantic layer, providing Tableau Next and Agentforce with a unified understanding of business data.' Concierge and Data Pro skills were slated for June 2025, Inspector 'in 2025'.
findings.source_title: Salesforce Redefines Business Intelligence with Tableau Next
findings.exact_quote: Tableau Next is now generally available with the Tableau+ SKU.

findings.claim: On 2026-05-05 Salesforce announced Tableau's 'Agentic Analytics Platform': Tableau Agent conversational analytics GA across Server, Cloud and Next; Tableau MCP servers GA; Teams, Slack and Google Workspace integrations GA; Command Center due in the fall.
findings.detail: Other quotes on the page: 'Tableau MCP servers are generally available for Tableau Next, Cloud, and Server.' 'Trusted by 97% of the Fortune 100'. 'it starts from 33 million semantic models built by the DataFam over more than a decade.' Page carries a forward-looking disclaimer that some features are unreleased. Marketing language; treat adoption figures as vendor claims.
findings.source_title: Tableau Unveils the Agentic Analytics Platform: Built on Trusted Knowledge
findings.exact_quote: Tableau Agent conversational analytics capabilities are generally available now, with new capabilities coming to dashboards in June.

findings.claim: Databricks AI/BI Genie went GA on 2025-06-12 after 4,000+ preview customers; on 2026-07-08 Genie Spaces were renamed Genie Agents, within a family of Genie One (business users), Genie Agents and Genie Code.
findings.detail: GA blog 2025-06-12: 'over 4000 customers adopted AI/BI Genie during its preview'. July 2026 release notes (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july): 'Genie Spaces are now called Genie Agents.' Genie docs (last updated 2026-09-18): 'Every answer is grounded in your organization's data and governed through Unity Catalog.' Genie One and Genie Agents usage is free through 2027-01-31. Genie One GA status not confirmed (index lists Public Preview). Semantic layer is Unity Catalog metric views.
findings.source_title: AI/BI Genie is now Generally Available
findings.exact_quote: AI/BI Genie is now generally available, enabling users to ask data questions in natural language and receive instant insights.

findings.claim: Snowflake now recommends moving from the standalone Cortex Analyst API to Cortex Agents (2026-08-28); the governed semantic views carry over unchanged. Cortex Agents and Snowflake Intelligence went GA 2025-11-04.
findings.detail: Release note 2026-08-28. Cortex Agents uses Cortex Analyst as its structured-data tool; the REST API remains available. Snowflake Intelligence GA release note: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2025/other/2025-11-04-snowflake-intelligence. Current docs render the product name as 'Snowflake CoWork' (rename date not found; medium confidence on the rename). Cortex Analyst docs: 'Semantic Views are the recommended approach'.
findings.source_title: Aug 28, 2026: Snowflake recommends transitioning from Cortex Analyst to Cortex Agents
findings.exact_quote: Your semantic views carry over unchanged. Cortex Agents uses the same semantic views for SQL generation, so you don't need to rebuild your semantic layer.

findings.claim: Looker Conversational Analytics is GA (since 2025); BigQuery Conversational Analytics and the Conversational Analytics API reached GA by July 2026. The LLM selects fields and filters while Looker composes and runs the query from the LookML model.
findings.detail: Status quote from Google Cloud blog 2026-07-28. Architecture from Looker docs (https://cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview, last updated 2026-09-18): 'Instead of querying your database directly, Conversational Analytics determines which fields, filters, sorts, and limits should be used in the query.' followed by 'Looker then composes and executes the query by using the underlying LookML model.' Dashboard Agents, Agentic Workflows and managed MCP server are preview (Next '26 post, 2026-04-22).
findings.source_title: Conversational analytics in Google Data Cloud in Q3 2026
findings.exact_quote: BigQuery Conversational Analytics and the Conversational Analytics API are now generally available, adding to the general availability of Conversational Analytics in Looker last year.

findings.claim: ThoughtSpot positions Spotter as deterministic and auditable because it translates questions into search tokens over a governed semantic layer rather than using LLM text-to-SQL.
findings.detail: Spotter product page (modified 2026-09-10), under the heading 'Deterministic Insights, Full Verifiability'. Spotter Semantics press release 2026-03-12 (Francois Lopitaux): 'Critically, this deterministic approach relies on our patented search tokens, not text-to-SQL powered by LLMs, which is why we can guarantee the most consistent, trustworthy insights on the market.' Adoption: 52% of customers using Spotter (2025-10-28 release), 'over 64%' (2026-03-12 release). Vendor claims.
findings.source_title: Spotter | The most trusted enterprise agent for analytics
findings.exact_quote: Instead of direct text-to-SQL, Spotter translates questions into search tokens grounded in your governed semantic layer—producing fully traceable, auditable queries.

findings.claim: The Open Semantic Interchange launched 2025-09-23 with 17 participants (Snowflake, Salesforce, dbt Labs, ThoughtSpot, BlackRock and others) to standardise semantic model exchange between AI agents and BI tools.
findings.detail: Snowflake blog by Josh Klahr, Khushboo Bhatia, Nick El-Rayess. Visible byline date Sep 23, 2025 (page JSON-LD says datePublished 2025-11-04; use the byline date). Kleinerman quote: 'to solve a foundational challenge for AI — the lack of a common semantic standard.'
findings.source_title: Snowflake Unites Industry Leaders to Unlock AI's Potential with the Open Semantic Interchange Initiative
findings.exact_quote: this vendor-agnostic standard ensures that your data's definitions and value remain consistent as they are interchanged between AI agents, BI platforms, and all other tools in your ecosystem

findings.claim: OSI entered the Apache Incubator on 2026-06-22 and was renamed Apache Ossie; the coalition grew from 17 to more than 50 organisations (now including Microsoft, Databricks, Qlik, Oracle), and the spec covers both semantic layer and ontology. The spec is still a 0.2.0 development draft.
findings.detail: Apache Incubator status page (https://incubator.apache.org/projects/ossie.html): '2026-06-22 Project enters incubation.' Rename post by Josh Klahr 2026-07-10: 'Ossie is an open specification for both semantic layer and ontology.' Working groups: Metric Language, Catalog, Ontology. Spec file in github.com/apache/ossie: 'DRAFT version — in development, schema may change before 0.2.0 is released.' Ecosystem list at https://ossie.apache.org/ecosystem/ (accessed 2026-09-21). Relevant to Article 4.
findings.source_title: Apache Ossie (Incubating): The New Name for Open Semantic Interchange
findings.exact_quote: The participating coalition has grown from 17 launch partners to more than 50 organizations

findings.claim: dbt Labs' April 2026 benchmark rerun: LLM answers routed through the dbt Semantic Layer scored 98.2% (Claude Sonnet 4.6) and 100% (GPT-5.3 Codex) versus 90.0% and 84.1% for raw text-to-SQL on the same modeled data; the semantic layer fails with an error rather than a plausible wrong number.
findings.detail: Jason Ganz and Benoit Perigaud, 2026-04-07. ACME Insurance benchmark (Sequeda et al.), 11 questions x 20 runs, open source (dbt-labs/dbt-llm-sl-bench). On the original normalized schema, in-scope questions: SL 100% vs text-to-SQL 62.5%/51.2%. Full-set text-to-SQL rose from 32.7% (2023) to 64.5% (2026), so the gap is narrowing. Caveats: vendor-run, small benchmark, text-to-SQL given the whole schema. Other quotes: 'With text-to-SQL, failure looks like a plausible but incorrect answer. With the Semantic Layer, failure looks like an error message.' and 'When accuracy matters (board data, auditors, OKRs, KPIs, weekly reports): configure a Semantic Layer and connect your LLM to it.'
findings.source_title: Semantic Layer vs. Text-to-SQL: 2026 Benchmark Update
findings.exact_quote: The Semantic Layer's deterministic query generation means the LLM can't produce subtly wrong results.

findings.claim: Google reports that Looker's semantic layer cuts gen AI natural-language query errors by as much as two thirds, and describes LookML calculations as deterministic.
findings.detail: Richard Kuzma and Jesse Sherb, 2025-05-07. Internal testing, methodology unpublished. Second quote: 'Deterministic advanced calculations: Ideal for complex mathematical or logistical operations, Looker eliminates randomness and provides predictable and repeatable outcomes.'
findings.source_title: How Looker's semantic layer enhances gen AI trustworthiness
findings.exact_quote: Our own internal testing has shown that Looker's semantic layer reduces data errors in gen AI natural language queries by as much as two thirds.

findings.claim: Older origin benchmarks (outside the 2025 to 2026 window): data.world found GPT-4 zero-shot accuracy on enterprise SQL of 16% rising to 54% over a knowledge graph (Nov 2023); Snowflake found GPT-4o at 51% on its internal BI set versus 90%+ for Cortex Analyst with a semantic model (Aug 2024).
findings.detail: arXiv 2311.07509, Sequeda, Allemang, Jacob, submitted 2023-11-13. Snowflake engineering blog 2024-08-29 (https://www.snowflake.com/en/engineering-blog/cortex-analyst-text-to-sql-accuracy-bi/): 'when we tested a state-of-the-art language model, GPT-4o, using our internal evaluation set, its accuracy plummeted to 51%.' Both predate the article's date window; use only as history.
findings.source_title: A Benchmark to Understand the Role of Knowledge Graphs on Large Language Model's Accuracy for Question Answering on Enterprise SQL Databases
findings.exact_quote: this accuracy increases to 54% when questions are posed over a Knowledge Graph representation of the enterprise SQL database.

findings.claim: The 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms was published 2026-06-29 (Ganeshan, Long, Macari). Google, ThoughtSpot and Qlik state they are Leaders; vendors frame the result around semantic layers grounding AI agents. No Gartner text was read directly.
findings.detail: Citation line confirmed on Qlik's reprint landing page (https://www.qlik.com/us/gartner-magic-quadrant-business-intelligence) and on Google's post. Google's own words, not Gartner's. ThoughtSpot press release 2026-07-01 (https://www.thoughtspot.com/press-releases/thoughtspot-named-a-leader-in-the-2026-gartner-magic-quadrant-for-analytics-and-bi-platforms): CEO says agents must 'generate trusted deterministic insights'. Microsoft and Tableau positions not verified (pages blocked).
findings.source_title: Google named a Leader in 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms for third year in a row
findings.exact_quote: we help ensure your autonomous AI agents operate on verified enterprise metrics, not hallucinated guesswork.

findings.claim: Forrester (Boris Evelson, July 2026) says natural-language data questions will arrive from many assistants and agents and must all be grounded in the same semantic layer, which should be treated as enterprise infrastructure; Forrester has opened coverage of semantic layer platforms (landscape Q4 2026, Wave Q1 2027).
findings.detail: Also: 'The organizations that succeed will be those that treat semantic layers and context graphs not as analytics features but as enterprise infrastructure for data, analytics, and AI.' Forrester does not use the word 'deterministic'.
findings.source_title: Multimodal, Semantic, And Agentic Enterprise Data Consumption Is The Future
findings.exact_quote: What matters is grounding them in the same semantic layer so that every agent interprets business terms, metrics, relationships, and context consistently.

findings.claim: Forrester (June 2026) argues agents without explicit semantic context guess and misinterpret metrics; the semantic layer is the right starting point and the knowledge graph or ontology the longer-term destination.
findings.detail: Boris Evelson with Indranil Bandyopadhyay, summarising two Forrester reports. Other quotes: 'Semantic layers have long ensured business-intelligence consistency. In the agentic era, they also give agents the governed context needed to turn natural language into accurate queries and actions.' and 'Most organizations are not yet ready to build a knowledge graph. The semantic layer is the right starting point.' A follow-up post (2026-08-20) defines a 'context layer' combining semantic layers with ontological modeling. Directly supports Article 4.
findings.source_title: Build Meaning Before Machines: Why Semantics, Ontologies, And Knowledge Graphs Matter For Agentic AI
findings.exact_quote: Without explicit context, they guess. And when agents guess, they get joins wrong, misinterpret metrics, and act on flawed assumptions.

findings.claim: Forrester's Q2 2025 BI Wave commentary: BI is not being replaced by generative AI; all BI vendors are integrating generative and agentic capabilities on the same LLMs.
findings.detail: Boris Evelson, 2025-04-10. Supports the 'BI is mature' claim. Headline points: 'BI is alive and well.' and 'GenAI is not the end of BI.'
findings.source_title: Key Takeaways From The Forrester Wave: Business Intelligence Platforms, Q2 2025
findings.exact_quote: BI continues to be a crucial enabler in the data-to-decisions process, which is essential for data-driven enterprises.

findings.claim: Tableau Pulse states plainly that the LLM does not compute: it narrates pre-calculated statistical insights produced by Tableau.
findings.detail: Tableau Pulse release notes, entry under 'Added July 2, 2026' announcing Tableau Agent in Pulse on GPT-5.2. The clearest 'platform computes, LLM explains' statement found. The URL pulse_intro.htm serves the page titled 'Tableau Pulse Release Notes'.
findings.source_title: Tableau Pulse Release Notes
findings.exact_quote: Note that this model doesn't analyze your data. Instead, it draws upon pre-calculated insights that are rooted in statistical analysis done by Tableau to answer questions about your metrics.

findings.claim: Microsoft Fabric IQ pairs the Power BI semantic model with an ontology item (still preview): ontologies can be generated from production semantic models so KPIs stay consistent across reports, agents and applications.
findings.detail: Microsoft Learn 'What is Fabric IQ?' (ms.date 2026-07-08). Also: 'Ontologies can be generated from existing Power BI semantic models, allowing you to bootstrap from trusted logic and definitions already in production.' Kim Manis, Fabric blog 2026-06-29: 'It provides a consistent semantic layer across data, allowing agents to work with business entities, relationships, rules, and metrics rather than disconnected tables and schemas.' Core evidence for Article 4 (BI working alongside the ontology).
findings.source_title: What is Fabric IQ?
findings.exact_quote: Semantic models and ontologies work together. You can generate or align ontologies directly from semantic models so terminology and KPIs stay consistent across reports, agents, and applications.

findings.claim: Microsoft adoption figures: more than 30 million monthly active Power BI and Fabric users and 25,000+ Fabric customers including about 80% of the Fortune 500 (Sept 2025); 35 million+ active users of semantic models and 31,000+ Fabric customers (March 2026).
findings.detail: Arun Ulag, FabCon Vienna post 2025-09-16; also 'more than 7 million actively building data visuals.' March 2026 figures from Azure Blog 2026-03-18 (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/fabcon-and-sqlcon-2026-unifying-databases-and-fabric-on-a-single-data-platform/): 'Already delivering insights to more than 35 million active users, semantic models provide the ideal foundation for training agents through Fabric IQ.' Vendor self-reported.

findings.exact_quote: With more than 30 million monthly active Power BI and Fabric users, it's already the default source of data and insights.

findings.claim: BI is being delivered inside collaboration and AI tools rather than only in BI portals: Tableau via MCP into Slack, Teams, Claude and ChatGPT; Tableau Pulse digests in Teams (Aug 2026); Genie in Slack, Teams, Excel and Sheets; PayPal scaled Looker conversational analytics to 3,000+ users through Claude Desktop.
findings.detail: Salesforce 2026-05-05 quote given. Tableau Pulse release notes 'Added August 26, 2026': 'Receive metric digests and alerts in Microsoft Teams'. Google 2026-07-01: 'PayPal, which successfully scaled accurate conversational analytics to 3,000+ users via Claude Desktop and Looker MCP.' Databricks release-note index: Slack app Public Preview (June 2026), Teams app Public Preview (July 2026), Excel and Google Sheets (Aug 2026). Power BI in Teams doc ms.date 2026-06-08.
findings.source_title: Tableau Unveils the Agentic Analytics Platform: Built on Trusted Knowledge
findings.exact_quote: Tableau's open MCP server architecture delivers trusted, context-grounded insights directly into Slack, Salesforce, Microsoft Teams, Claude, ChatGPT, and any other surface where your teams work.

findings.claim: Forrester's baseline for the widening-audience argument: hands-on BI use has been stuck at roughly 20% of decision-makers; natural language, ML alerting and embedded analytics are the routes to the other 80%.
findings.detail: Boris Evelson, 2024-07-01, outside the 2025 to 2026 window, so use as background only. He predicts natural language adds about 10%, ML alerting about 20%, embedded or ambient analytics the remainder. ThoughtSpot (2025-10-28) relays an unverified Gartner prediction that 'by 2026, over 80% of business consumers will prefer intelligence assistance and embedded analytics over traditional dashboards' (second-hand, not checked against Gartner).
findings.source_title: Bring Data To The Other 80% Of Business Intelligence Users
findings.exact_quote: out of all enterprise decision-makers who could and should be using analytical applications and platforms hands-on, only 20% do so today.

findings.claim: Microsoft documents a threshold-to-workflow chain: Power BI data alerts trigger Power Automate flows, and Fabric Activator turns rule conditions on streams or Power BI report visuals into emails, Teams messages, Power Automate flows, pipelines and notebooks.
findings.detail: Activator intro (ms.date 2026-04-17): 'Fabric Activator is a no-code event detection engine that transforms data streams into automated actions.' Power BI is listed as an event source 'for Activator rules on report visuals'. Power Automate integration doc (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-flow-integration, ms.date 2025-12-01): 'use a template to create a flow that's triggered by a Power BI data alert (notification).' Dashboard alerts doc (ms.date 2026-08-24): 'You can automate and integrate alerts with Power Automate.' Limits: dashboard alerts only on gauges, KPIs and cards, and only on refreshed data. Fabric operations agents (ms.date 2026-08-03) monitor real-time data and recommend actions.
findings.source_title: What is Fabric Activator?
findings.exact_quote: These actions can include sending emails or Teams notifications, launching Power Automate flows, or integrating with third-party systems.

findings.claim: Looker Agentic Workflows (preview, July 2026) let a user set a metric threshold in chat; when crossed, a background agent runs key driver analysis and posts the diagnosis to Slack or email.
findings.detail: Google Cloud blog 2026-07-29. Preview for Looker 26.08+. Example prompts on the page: 'Monitor return rates weekly' and 'Notify me if average order value exceeds $1,000.' Administrators keep oversight of all workflows.
findings.source_title: Looker adds agentic workflows for data monitoring and insights

findings.claim: Tableau and ThoughtSpot both document insight-to-action triggers: Tableau Pulse alerts on unfavourable threshold crossings, Tableau Next dashboards invoke Salesforce Flows, and Spotter creates Jira tickets, updates Salesforce and triggers enterprise workflows.
findings.detail: Tableau Next overview (help.tableau.com, undated, accessed 2026-09-21). Tableau Pulse release notes: 'You receive an alert when a metric that you're following crosses into an unfavorable threshold range or has a new unfavorable trend.' Salesforce 2026-05-05: 'Tableau's decision engine turns insights into decision and actions, directly triggering workflows so every person and every agent can act on what the data is telling them.' ThoughtSpot Spotter page: 'Turns insights into action by automatically creating Jira tickets, updating Salesforce opportunities, posting to Slack, or triggering workflows in enterprise systems.' Forrester 2026-07-23 describes the same pattern as 'agentic-based subscription analytics'.

findings.detail: BARC commentary 2025-11-12; Trend Monitor 2026 summary pages dated 2026-01-16 to 2026-02-02. Full report gated and not read. No BARC statement found framing BI metrics as the deterministic layer for agents. Other quote: 'data quality management has returned to the number one spot'.
findings.source_title: Data quality beats AI hype

findings.claim: dbt Labs states the 'agent calls the governed metric' pattern explicitly through its MCP server: the agent returns the defined metric rather than deriving its own.
findings.detail: dbt Developer Blog 2026-07-23. MCP tools list_metrics, get_dimensions, query_metrics sit beside a separate text_to_sql tool. dbt blog 2026-09-16 (https://docs.getdbt.com/blog/dbt-context-engineering): 'an agent can pull a governed, tested metric through the semantic layer today.' Microsoft equivalent: Power BI MCP servers doc (ms.date 2026-09-01) says agents 'discover and call tools to author and query Power BI semantic models and reports.'
