Client list, the authenticated/permission-bound/fully logged sentence, the single-connection sentence and the 32% Knowledge Work Benchmark Report 2026 figure all verbatim. 'general availability' and 'read-only' absent.

verdicts.claim: LawVu's MCP server announcement is dated 2026-06-02 (updated 2026-06-08) and states write actions for the initial release: creating matters, triggering contract workflows, updating matter status, creating tasks and setting deadlines.
verdicts.corrected_detail: A Wayback capture does exist, at 20260608210141 (2026-06-08T21:01Z), taken after the page's modified time of 2026-06-08T10:46+12:00; the finding said none exists. The live URL returns HTTP 403 to plain curl but loads via a normal fetcher.
verdicts.note: Content confirmed from the capture and the live page: Sam Kidd; published_time 2026-06-02T08:00+12:00; modified_time 2026-06-08T10:46+12:00; 'Updated June 8, 2026'; the 'In the initial release ... will enable' list with both write bullets verbatim; clients Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot; governance wording; 'Customers can now bring tools like Claude and ChatGPT'; no GA wording.

verdicts.claim: Anthropic's Claude for Legal launch page (2026-05-12) describes the Box connector with the write verbs 'create or update content', Datasite with 'set up folder structures, invite users', and Relativity with 'stand up matters, shape workspace schema, govern access'; these are Anthropic's descriptions.
verdicts.corrected_detail: A Wayback capture exists at 20260715141014; the finding said none exists. The page also carries a post-publication dateModified: 'Jun 21, 2026' in the 2026-07-15 capture and 'Jul 20, 2026' on the live page today. The quoted connector descriptions are identical in both versions, but no capture predates 2026-06-21, so the exact wording is proven only from 2026-06-21 onward; a strict usable_by would be 2026-06-21 rather than 2026-06-14.
verdicts.note: All quoted Box, Datasite, Relativity, Docusign, iManage and NetDocuments descriptions and the '20+ new MCP connectors ... 12 new plugins' sentence are verbatim in the 2026-07-15 capture and the live page. datePublished May 12, 2026 in both.

verdicts.claim: The Gartner press release of 2026-05-11 is confirmed from gartner.com itself through a Wayback capture of 2026-07-09, and the primary states that Rita Sallam was speaking at the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in London, which the IT-Online mirror omitted.
verdicts.note: Capture 20260709022118 fetched: dateline LONDON, U.K., May 11, 2026; 'Speaking at the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in London today, Rita Sallam, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, said:' followed by the quote; summit May 11-13 in London. An earlier capture at 20260519122104 has identical text and is a better date-discipline anchor. Could not see the earlier verified note being corrected, but the primary supports both attributions.

verdicts.claim: Gartner's prediction (up to 80% higher agentic AI accuracy and up to 60% lower cost by 2027 for organizations that prioritize semantics) and its advice to establish a context layer are verbatim on the gartner.com primary.
verdicts.note: Prediction sentence, context-layer advice, schema-based-models sentence and the Sallam 'cost-control and trust strategy' quote all verbatim in both the 2026-05-19 and 2026-07-09 captures. Framed as a Gartner prediction.

verdicts.claim: The MCP specification revision of 2025-06-18 classified MCP servers as OAuth resource servers, required clients to implement RFC 8707 resource indicators, and added a security best practices page; authorization is optional in the protocol.
verdicts.note: Changelog 2025-06-18 lists all three items verbatim (PR #338, PR #734). Authorization page: 'Authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations.' and 'Authorization servers MUST implement OAuth 2.1 with appropriate security'. GitHub history of authorization.mdx: created 2025-06-18 (d2cac4fd14), last edit 2025-09-23 (prettier), intermediate commits are link and wording fixes.

verdicts.claim: The MCP specification (2025-06-18) says there should always be a human in the loop able to deny tool invocations, that applications should present confirmation prompts, and that clients must treat tool annotations as untrusted unless the server is trusted.
verdicts.note: All three sentences verbatim on the live tools page and in the original 2025-06-18 revision of tools.mdx (d2cac4fd14). The file was edited as late as 2026-07-20 for an unrelated structuredContent clarification.

verdicts.claim: The MCP security best practices document (2025-06-18 version) is addressed to implementers, server operators and security professionals, covers the confused deputy problem, token passthrough and session hijacking, and states that token passthrough is forbidden; the live URL now redirects to a later living page.
verdicts.note: Raw file at d1935d2ce9 (2025-08-11, prettier-only) has the audience sentence verbatim, the three attack sections, and 'Token passthrough is explicitly forbidden in the [authorization specification] as it introduces a number of security risks'. Created d2cac4fd14 2025-06-18; removed fcc57c725e 2026-03-25 whose message names docs/tutorials/security/security_best_practices. Live URL returns 308 to /docs/2025-11-25/tutorials/security/security_best_practices, the versioned path of that living page.

verdicts.claim: The MCP specification revision of 2025-11-25 added OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents as the recommended client registration mechanism, incremental scope consent, default scopes, client security requirements for local server installation, and an updated Security Best Practices page, and introduced extensions including authorization extensions.
verdicts.note: Changelog 2025-11-25: SEP-991 CIMD sentence, SEP-835 incremental scope consent, 'Updated the Security Best Practices guidance.' verbatim. Anniversary post (published 2025-11-25, modified 2026-03-12): 'SEP-1024: Client security requirements for local server installation', 'SEP-835: Default scopes definition in authorization specification', 'SEP-1046: OAuth client credentials support for machine-to-machine authorization', Extensions and Authorization Extensions sections with Optional / Additive / Composable / Versioned independently, and the 'not just a hobby protocol' sentence verbatim.

verdicts.claim: The authorization hardening of the 2026-07-28 MCP specification was published as a release candidate on 2026-05-21, so the point can be kept under a 2026-07-14 display date as a release candidate due to become final on 28 July 2026.
verdicts.note: Live post: published_time 2026-05-21T09:00Z, modified 2026-07-24. Wayback capture 20260716064405 (modified_time 2026-05-22) already contains every quoted sentence: locked as of May 21, final on July 28, 'Six SEPs harden...', the iss / RFC 9207 (SEP-2468) sentence, the mix-up attack sentence, stateless core, Extensions, Tasks, MCP Apps and the twelve-month deprecation lifecycle. Text proven as of 2026-05-22 at the latest.

verdicts.claim: The Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension to MCP was declared stable on 2026-06-18, with Anthropic, Microsoft and Okta among adopters and Okta as the first supported identity provider; this confirms from the primary that EMA pre-dates the 2026-07-28 release.
verdicts.note: Post dated June 18, 2026 by Paul Carleton (Core Maintainer), published_time 2026-06-18T17:00Z. Verbatim: 'The Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) extension is now stable.'; 'being adopted by Anthropic, Microsoft, Okta and a growing number of MCP servers'; 'Okta is the first supported identity provider.'; 'Anthropic has implemented the extension in its shared MCP layer for Claude.'; the centralized policy and audit bullet. Wayback capture 20260619180351 exists.

verdicts.claim: An MCP maintainers' post of 2026-03-16 states that tool annotations such as read-only and destructive are hints that clients must treat as untrusted, that a tool with no annotations is assumed potentially destructive, and that clients vary in how strictly they honour the defaults; this is a pre-cutoff primary statement of the responsibilities the protocol leaves to clients and operators.
verdicts.note: Post published_time 2026-03-16 (modified 2026-03-18), authors Ola Hungerford, Sam Morrow, Luca Chang. All four quoted passages verbatim.

verdicts.claim: The Build 2026 blog describes the three layers of Fabric IQ in its own words and defines the operational layer as ontologies that capture operational context by defining business entities and their relationships so agents can reason in the language of the business.
verdicts.note: 2026-06-13 capture: 'It provides three integrated layers of business context:' followed by the Unified data, Business intelligence and Operational intelligence bullets exactly as quoted.
